money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Romanian Leu (RON). Romania is a member of the European Union (EU). Declare cash over 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Romania and non-EU countries. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you don't declare or give incorrect information, you'll need to pay a fine. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country. Romania is largely a cash economy. However, credit card and debit card use is increasing. It's illegal to change money on the streets. Exchange money at banks, large hotels or exchange burea

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They can include prison sentences of up to 20 years.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Surrogacy is not legally recognised and unregulated in Romania. The Australian Embassy can't provide: legal advice about surrogacy information on clinics
laws.heading: Surrogacy

laws.rule: Always carry a photo ID. Keep your passport in a safe place and carry a photocopy. In Romania, it's illegal to: take photos of airports, military sites or other secure locations engage in sex work or pay for sexual services have sexual relationships with a person under 16.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: To drive a vehicle, you'll need a current Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted). If you hold a valid Australian driver's licence, you can drive for up to 6 months from your arrival in Romania. Your licence must be valid for the type of vehicle you'll drive. You could face a large fine if you don't have the correct licence. Your insurance won't cover you if you have an accident.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Romania is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Get an entry stamp at the first Schengen entry.
